corrections.why: The Coast Guard list gives the structure as 19.2 m above ground; the 24.4 m figure is the focal height of the light above the water.

resolved_conflicts.explanation: The municipality says the year 1880 is cut in the cornerstone; LighthouseFriends says the tower began operation in 1881 after the 1878 appropriation and the contract was annulled. The record keeps 1881 as first_lit; the cornerstone year is in the story and the event note.

The municipality gives the tower as 24.4 m (74 ft); the Coast Guard gives 19.2 m above ground and 24.4 m as the focal height. The record's 19.0 m is corrected to 19.2 m; the municipal figure is noted in the story.

The municipality says the lamp was electric from 1922; LighthouseFriends says the range lights were electrified in 1925. Both are kept, since the lamp and the range lights may have changed at different times.

The municipality and LighthouseFriends describe a two-storey house; the Canadian Register describes an attached one-and-a-half storey, gable-roofed dwelling. The story states both sources' descriptions in the text.

notes_for_editor: (1) Build date: the municipality's cornerstone reads 1880; LighthouseFriends and the record say 1881 (lit). Both are in the story. (2) The 1874-1881 history (pier light, 1877 inspection, 1878 appropriation, the Joseph White contract, the 1885 letter) is from LighthouseFriends only; it quotes Canadian reports that are not in our corpus. Not checked against a primary copy. The 1877 quotations are as LighthouseFriends gives them. (3) The Anna Maria date is inferred: the Cleveland Gazette dispatch (dated 9 October 1902) says 'Tuesday night', which is 7 October 1902; LighthouseFriends gives 7 October too. (4) The Gazette OCR garbles the list of the dead. The story gives only the count of five, which both sources agree on, and the dispatch's names (captain, three of the crew, Mr. Ferguson). LighthouseFriends names different dead (captain, a female cook, two other crew, one rescuer). The two accounts agree on the count and disagree on who the dead were. (5) The rewards list (Appendix No. 16, printed p. 228) spells the schooner 'Anne Maria' and matches the Kincardine rescue row to a names column by position in OCR text. The volunteer crew list naming 'W. H. Ferguson (drowned)' is NOT used in the story, because the match to this rescue is by position only. The page image should be checked before anyone uses it. (6) The St. Paul Globe OCR garbles the medal sentence (the metal of the medals is unreadable); the story says only 'medals' and quotes the clean phrase. (7) PAGES: the Singapore entry is on printed p. 8 (scan p. 21). The OCR index read the page as p. 3, which the page image corrects: the image shows the header '8 MARINE AND FISHERIES'. The 1911 Kincardine light entry is in the Commissioner of Lights section, printed p. 77 (scan p. 84); the page image confirms the header 'REPORT OF THE COMMISSIONER OF LIGHTS 77'. The 1903 life-saving station entry (Chief Engineer's volume, FY ended 30 June 1903) is on printed p. 25 (Deputy Minister's report, scan p. 38). The 1903 front tower (33 ft) is on printed p. 48 (scan p. 61). The fog siren is on printed p. 45. The 1910 'No wrecks' entry is on printed p. 204 (life-saving list, after the page header '204 MARINE AND FISHERIES'). The 1902 burning is on printed p. 62 (scan p. 75). The 1900 harbour survey is on printed p. 68 (scan p. 83), in the Officer in Charge of the Hydrographic Survey's report. (8) Burley (1956 to 1978) and the 1977 end of the keeper job disagree within LighthouseFriends (roster versus text); the story states both. Burley's connection ended after 1960, so only his name and years appear. (9) The 1903 steel front light is no longer the front light; the Coast Guard lists a 6.1 m mast. (10) Phantom Piper legend: presented as tradition, as the municipality and LighthouseFriends tell it. (11) The life-saving station crew (Thomas McGaw as coxswain; the 1902 volunteer crew) belongs to the life-saving station record, not this lighthouse roster; McGaw is listed here as the keeper who was also coxswain. (12) The Canadian Register describes the attached dwelling as one-and-a-half storeys; the municipality and LighthouseFriends say two. The story states the disagreement. (13) The tower height disagrees: the municipality gives 24.4 m (74 ft) tall; LighthouseFriends and the Coast Guard give 19.2 m (63 ft) for the structure, with 24.4 m as the focal height. The story states both. (14) The Rowlett directory listed in the record was not read.
